trajectories.input: Towns in the eastern Dominican Republic began making preparations for tens of thousands of refugees, and by 16 January hospitals near the border had been filled beyond capacity with Haitians. By 17 January some reported that they had exhausted supplies of essential medical materials such as antibiotics. Dominican soldiers reinforced the border, and the Dominican Republic's government declared that any Haitians who crossed for medical care would be permitted to remain only on a temporary basis. A local governor remarked, "We have a great desire and we will do everything humanly possible to help Haitian families. But we have our limitations with respect to food and medicine. We need the helping hand of other countries in the area."

trajectories.input: A great deal of Sholay was filmed in the rocky landscape around Ramanagara, a town near Bangalore in Karnataka. To reach the sets more easily, the filmmakers had to construct a road linking the Bangalore highway to Ramanagara. Art director Ram Yedekar erected an entire township on the location. A prison set was also built outdoors near Rajkamal Studio in Mumbai so that its natural lighting would match that of the on-location shoots. For a time, one section of Ramanagara was known as "Sippy Nagar" in honor of the film's director. As of 2010, tourists passing through Ramanagara were still offered a visit to the "Sholay rocks," where much of the film was shot.
